newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine sugar import ban extended to July 1997.
newsitem.headline: Philippine sugar import ban extended to July 1997.

text.p: The Philippine Sugar Regulatory Administration chief Wilson Gamboa said on Wednesday he had ordered an extension of the country's sugar import ban to July this year.
In October last year, Gamboa had asked traders and millers to stop sugar imports up to March this year.
The order was issued to ensure that the large stocks of sugar in the country's warehouses were exhausted.
"We have decided to extend the sugar importation ban to July, at which time we expect the glut to have eased," Gamboa told reporters at a news conference.

The domestic sugar glut was due to the importation of 1.023 million tonnes of sugar from neighbouring countries in crop year 1995-1996 (Sept-Aug) against production shortfalls of 500,000 tonnes, Gamboa said.

Domestic sugar prices dropped to a low of 480 pesos three months ago from a high of 800 to 900 pesos at the start of 1996 because of the surge in supply between December 1996 and March 1997, the peak milling months in the Philippines when at least 1.2 million tonnes of sugar was added to existing supplies.
Gamboa said Philippine sugar millers, including the trading arm of Victorias Milling Corp, have unsold stocks of 100,000 tonnes of sugar in their warehouses.
The Victorias unit, North Negros Marketing Corp, has sought approval to sell 27,000 tonnes of refined sugar, he said.
The company has incurred at least 100 million pesos in carrying costs on its sugar stocks in the past 10 months, he added.
Other mills that have unsold raw sugar in their warehouses include New Frontier with 47,000 tonnes and San Carlos Milling with 6,000 tonnes, he said.
Gamboa said he had asked New Frontier to convert its raw stocks to refined sugar to prolong its shelf life.
